- **Step 8-pre-ship — phantom untracked files:** 3 file(s) appeared since session baseline (inspect <TMPDIR>/phantom-paths-8-pre-ship.z locally)

- Deviation from G-Cfg-1 (define every wire/path literal once): the change establishes the module-private constant `PYTHON_PREFIX = "python/"` in the three sibling ports `python/larch/lint/lint_env_via_config_constant.py`, `python/larch/lint/lint_lifecycle_prefix_literal.py`, and `python/larch/lint/lint_subprocess_via_runner.py`, and routes every scan filter, detector `removeprefix`, and `to_engine_finding` path render through it. The fourth port in the same change, `python/larch/lint/lint_suppression_reason.py`, does not define the constant and instead inlines the literal `"python/"` at three sites: `is_production_source_path` (`rel_path.startswith("python/")` and `rel_path[len("python/"):]`), `detect` (`source.path.removeprefix("python/")`), and `to_engine_finding` (`path=f"python/{finding.file}"`). That rendered path is the finding identity the engine persists into `suppression-reason-baseline.json`, so the literal is a wire/path literal of the kind G-Cfg-1 covers, and the three call sites exceed the "one call site with no cross-module contract" deviation clause. To resolve, add `PYTHON_PREFIX = "python/"` to `lint_suppression_reason.py` and route the three sites through it, matching the sibling ports landed in this same change. No other guideline deviations identified: G-Dup-1 is satisfied (the change collapses four duplicated baseline-I/O / duplicate-detection / write-check owners into the shared engine); G-Enf-2 is satisfied (the engine-adoption baseline only shrinks, removing rows whose modules no longer violate); G-Wire-3 is satisfied (engine.py gained two fields and all four rule definitions, their tests, and the adoption baseline were swept in the same change).
